Rashi on Eruvin 103a:11:1.hebrew: אמר לך בכלי - למה לי לאשמועינן בפסחים דאסור? הא כבר שמעינן לה הכא, ולמה ליה לתנא לסתמיה בתרי דוכתי:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:11:1.english: He can say to you: With an instrument - Why do I need [the Mishnah] to teach us in [tractate] Pesachim that it is forbidden? Behold, we have already learned it here, and why would the Tanna teach it anonymously in two places?

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:12:1.hebrew: ואידך - להכי הדר תניא התם, משום פלוגתא דרבי אליעזר, דאשמועינן דאפילו בכלי שרי:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:12:1.english: And the other [Sage] - For this reason it is taught again there: because of the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer, to inform us that even with an implement it is permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:13:1.hebrew: ואידך - להכי לא מוקמינן לההיא דפסחים בלחה ובכלי, דאם כן — הוה ליה אב מלאכה, והתם — הא דשבות הוא דאיירי:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:13:1.english: And the other [Sage] - That is why we do not interpret that [mishnah] in Pesachim as [referring to a wart that is] moist and [cut] with an instrument — because if so, it would be a primary category of labor, whereas there, it is only dealing with [matters of] rabbinic prohibition [shevut].

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:13:2.hebrew: דומיא דהרכיבו - דלא מיתסר אלא מדרבנן, דחי נושא עצמו, ותחומין נמי דרבנן. ואפ"ה, הואיל ואפשר מאתמול — לא דחי:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:13:2.english: Parallel to carrying it - Which is prohibited only by rabbinic law, for a living being carries itself; and [the prohibition of] boundaries is also rabbinic. And even so, since it was possible [to do it] yesterday, it does not override [Shabbat].

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:14:1.hebrew: ואידך - הרכיבו והבאתו גופה מלאכה גמורה היא, דלא ס"ל להאי תנא בפסחים כר' נתן, דאמר במס' שבת בפ' המצניע (שבת דף צד.): "חי נושא את עצמו", ובתחומין סבר לה כרבי עקיבא, דאמר במס' סוטה בפרק כשם שהמים בודקין (דף כז:): "תחומין דאורייתא":
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:14:1.english: And the other [Sage] - [Maintains that] carrying it and bringing it is itself a full [Torah] labor, as this Tanna in Pesachim does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Natan, who said in tractate Shabbat in the chapter [entitled] Hamatznia (Shabbat 94a): "A living being carries itself"; and regarding [Shabbat] boundaries he holds in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who said in tractate Sotah in the chapter [entitled] Keshem Shehamayim Bodkin (27b): "[The prohibition of Shabbat] boundaries is from the Torah."

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:15:1.hebrew: א"ר אליעזר ק"ו - התם גבי פלוגתייהו תנינן לה, בפ' אלו דברים (פסחים סה:):
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:15:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer said: An a fortiori inference - There, regarding their dispute, we learned it in the chapter [entitled] Elu Devarim (Pesachim 65b).

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:15:2.hebrew: אלו שמשום שבות - אלמא ת"ק משום שבות קא אסר להו, וש"מ דלאו בכלי מתוקמא:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:15:2.english: These, which are due to rabbinic decree - Evidently, the first tanna prohibited them due to a rabbinic decree, and conclude from this that [the mishnah] is not established [as referring to cutting] with an implement.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:16:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רב יוסף הא והא ביד - ומיהו מתני' ביבישה לא מוקמינן לה, דאם כן, אפילו בכלי שרי. אלא בלחה וביד, היינו טעמא דשרי — דשבות הוא, ובמקדש; שתמידין וקרבנות צבור במקדש הם מבקרין אותן. ובפסחים, היינו טעמא דאסור — דאע"ג דשבות הוא וצורך מקדש הוא, אפ"ה, כיון דכל אחד ואחד מבקר פסחו ומתקנו בביתו ואח"כ מביאו למקדש, לא התירו לעבור על השבות במדינה:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:16:1.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said: Both are by hand - However, we do not establish our Mishnah [as dealing] with a dry [wart], for if so, it would be permitted even with an implement. Rather, [it deals] with a moist [wart] and by hand; [and] this is the reason that it is permitted: for it is a rabbinic prohibition, and in the Temple — as the daily offerings and communal sacrifices, they inspect them in the Temple. And with regard to Paschal offerings, this is the reason that it is forbidden: for even though it is a rabbinic prohibition and a need of the Temple, even so, since each and every person inspects his Paschal offering and prepares it in his house and afterward brings it to the Temple, they did not permit violating a rabbinic prohibition in the country.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:17:1.english: This teaching - That of Rav Yosef.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:17:2.hebrew: גוללו אצלו - דכיון דאיגדו בידו, אע"ג דאיכא שבות דילמא נפיל כוליה לרה"ר ואתי לאיתויי — ספר נמי שבות דמקדש קרי ליה, שהרי קדש הוא. אלמא, שבות דצורך מקדש הותר אף במדינה:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:17:2.english: He rolls it to himself - For since its attachment is in his hand, even though there is a rabbinic prohibition — lest it fall completely into the public domain and he come to bring it [in] — [the Gemara] also calls a scroll a “rabbinic prohibition of the Temple,” since it is sacred. Evidently, a rabbinic prohibition for the need of the Temple was permitted even in the provinces.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:18:1.hebrew: הא אוקימנא - בריש פירקין, באסקופה כרמלית וכו', דאפילו שבות ליכא למגזר; דא"נ נפיל כוליה, כי ממטי ליה לתוך הבית דרך האסקופה — אין כאן חיוב חטאת:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:18:1.english: Didn't we establish it - At the beginning of our chapter, [as referring to] a threshold that is a karmelit, etc., that there is not even [reason] to decree a rabbinic prohibition; for even if all of it falls, when he brings it into the house via the threshold, there is no liability for a sin-offering here:

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:19:1.hebrew: משלשלין וכו' - לצלותו, והוא יצלה מעצמו. ובבשר דעלמא אמרינן: אין צולין בשר, בצל וביצה אלא כדי שיצולו מבעוד יום — גזירה שמא יחתה בגחלים, בפ"ק דשבת (יט:):
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:19:1.english: One may lower, etc. - To roast it, and it will roast on its own. And regarding ordinary meat we say: One may not roast meat, an onion, or an egg unless [there is enough time] for them to roast while it is still day — [as a] decree lest one rake the coals — in the first chapter of Shabbat (19b).

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:19:2.hebrew: והא הכא - דכל אחד צולה פסחו בביתו, וקשרי ליה נמי במדינה:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:19:2.english: But here - For each person roasts his Paschal offering in his home, and [the Mishnah] permits it in the province as well.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:1:1.hebrew: אי אליבא דר"א קאמר - כלומר, כמאן ס"ל במכשירין? על כרחך כר"א ס"ל, וכיון דכר"א ס"ל — אמאי הוי לכתחילה אסור:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:1:1.english: If he stated [his ruling] in accordance with [the opinion of] Rabbi Eliezer - That is to say: In accordance with whose [opinion] does he hold regarding [mitzvah] preparations? Perforce he holds in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer. And since he holds in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, why is it forbidden ab initio?

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:21:1.hebrew: בני חבורה - הנמנין על הפסח זריזין הן, דכל העוסקין בקדשים זריזין וחכמים. הלכך, לא מחתי:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:21:1.english: Members of a group - Those registered for the Paschal offering are vigilant, for all who are involved with sacrificial offerings are vigilant and wise; therefore, they will not rake [the coals].

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:21:2.hebrew: ואביי - דאישתיק, סבר: "כהנים זריזין הן" אמרינן בכמה דוכתי, דכיון שנכנס לעבודה בידוע שלמדוהו הלכות קדש; אבל "בני חבורה זריזין הן" לא אמרינן, שאין לך אדם שאינו עושה פסח:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:21:2.english: And Abaye - [The reason] that he remained silent [is that] he held: We say “priests are vigilant” in several places, for once [a priest] enters into the [Temple] service, it is known that they taught him the laws of consecrated items; but we do not say “members of a group are vigilant,” for there is no person who does not make the Passover [offering].

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:22:1.hebrew: רבא אמר - הא והא ביד, כדאמר, דבכלי ליכא לאוקמי לפסחים משום מלאכה; והא והא בלחה, דאי ביבישה לא מיתסר בכלי. אלא מתני' דקתני שבות דאפשר לה מאתמול מידחי מקמי מכשירי מצוה — ר"א היא, דפליג נמי עלה דההוא דפסחים, ואמר: דוחין, דאפילו אב מלאכה מידחי מקמייהו, וכ"ש שבות. והא דקתני במתני' דבכלי אסור — מודה ר"א דכמה דאפשר לשנויי משנינן ליה, ולא מחללינן שבתא; והיכא דלא אפשר, כגון גבי איזמל, דחינן אפילו אב מלאכה:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:22:1.english: Rava said - Both this [mishnah] and that [mishnah are discussing removing the wart] by hand, as [the Gemara] said, for the [mishnah of] Pesachim cannot be established [as referring to doing so] with an instrument because of [the Torah] labor; and both this and that [mishnah are discussing] a soft [wart], for if [it were] dry, it would not be forbidden [even] with an instrument. Rather, our Mishnah, which teaches that a rabbinic prohibition that could have been done yesterday is overridden in the face of preparations for a mitzvah, is [the view of] Rabbi Eliezer, who also disagrees with that [mishnah] of Pesachim and says [preparations] override [Shabbat], for even a primary category of labor is overridden in their face, and all the more so a rabbinic prohibition. And that which is taught in our Mishnah, that with an instrument it is forbidden — Rabbi Eliezer concedes that as much as it is possible to alter [the manner of performance], we alter it and do not desecrate Shabbat; and where it is not possible [to alter], such as in the case of a [circumcision] knife, we override even a primary category of labor.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:2:1.hebrew: אלא הא ר' שמעון והא רבנן - מתני' — רבנן, דפליגי עליה דר"ש ואמרי קושרה, דסבירא להו כר"א בחדא: דמכשירי מצוה דוחין וכו', וכגון בשאי אפשר לעשות מאתמול, כדקתני "שנפסקה לו נימא בכנורו", ופליגי עליה בשאפשר לעשות מבעוד יום; הלכך, בתחילה אסור. ומעיקרא, כי הוה מוקמינן לה כר' יהודה, מ"ט לא שנינן הכי? משום דלא שמעינן בהדיא דאית ליה האי סברא למפלג בין אפשר לאי אפשר, וכל כמה דלא אשכח תנא דאמר הכי בהדיא, מיבעיא לן סתמא דמתניתין מני:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:2:1.english: Rather, this is Rabbi Shimon and that is the Rabbis - The Mishnah is according to the Rabbis, who disagree with Rabbi Shimon and say that he may tie it. For they hold in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer in one respect, that the preparations for a mitzvah override Shabbat, etc., namely where it was impossible to perform them from yesterday, as it teaches: "A string of his harp was severed"; and they disagree with him where it was possible to perform them while it was still day. Therefore, initially it is forbidden. And initially, when we were establishing it in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, what is the reason we did not answer in this way? Because we did not hear explicitly that he holds this reasoning, to distinguish between where it was possible and where it was impossible; and as long as the Gemara had not found a Tanna who said this explicitly, we asked: In accordance with whose opinion is the anonymous Mishnah?

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:3:1.hebrew: אף היא - אם היה עונבה או קושרה, אינה משמעת את הקול. והואיל וקשירה נמי אב מלאכה היא, הא עדיפא, שתשמיע את הקול. וטוב לנו לחלל את השבת בשלשולו לקיים השמעת קול שיר של לוים, מלחלל שבת בקשירה, שהיא אב מלאכה, ולא נקיים בה שום מצוה, דלא מצי השמע קול:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:3:1.english: Even it - If he were to tie a bow in it or knot it, it will not issue the [proper] sound. And since knotting is also a primary category of labor, this is preferable, so that it will issue the sound. And it is better for us to desecrate Shabbat by unwinding it in order to fulfill the sounding of the song of the Levites, than to desecrate Shabbat by knotting, which is a primary category of labor and [where] we would not fulfill any mitzvah through it, since it cannot produce sound.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:3:2.hebrew: משלשל מלמטה וכורך מלמעלה - שהרי יש יתדות מלמעלה ולמטה שראשי הנימין כרוכין בהן, וכשהוא רוצה מגלגל היתד והנימא נארכת, כעין שעושין למיני כלי זמר — ארפ"א — דמאריך עד שיגיע ליתד שלמעלה וכורכה בו, והרי היא כבתחלה, ומגלגלין היתד עד שמתפשטת כהלכתה ומשמעת קולה. ולרבנן, עדיפא למשרי קשירה, דהא משלשל נמי אב מלאכה הוא, דמתקן כלי כהלכתו, וכיון (דדמי) [דשרי] לכתחלה — מחליף, ואתי נמי להתיר נימין בכנור חדש לכתחלה, הלכך קשירה עדיפא:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:3:2.english: He unwinds from below and winds from above - For there are pegs above and below around which the ends of the strings are wound, and when he wishes, he turns the peg and the string lengthens, similar to what is done with types of musical instruments — harpe [harp] — so that he lengthens [it] until it reaches the peg above and winds it around it, and it is then as [it was] at the beginning; and they turn the peg until [the string] is properly taut and produces its sound. And according to the Rabbis, it is preferable to permit tying, for unwinding is also a primary category of labor, as it repairs a vessel properly; and since [it would be] permitted ab initio, one might confuse [the cases] and come to attach strings to a new harp ab initio as well; therefore, tying is preferable.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:4:1.hebrew: הא והא רבנן - דמכשירין שא"א מבעוד יום דוחין. והא דקתני מתניתין קושרה — כשנפסקה באמצעית, שאילמלי עונבה לא תשמע קולה; והא דקתני עונבה — כשנפסקה בראשיה, שאין צריכה שם חיזוק כל כך, וסגי ליה בעניבה:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:4:1.english: Both this and that are the Rabbis - For [they maintain that mitzva] preparations that cannot [be performed] while it is yet day override [Shabbat]. And that which the Mishnah teaches, “[one] ties it,” [is] when it was severed in its middle, for if he [merely] tied it in a bow, its sound would not be heard; and that which [the baraita] teaches, “[one] ties it in a bow,” [is] when it was severed at its ends, where it does not require so much tightening, and a bow is sufficient for it.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:5:1.hebrew: ואי בעית אימא הא והא באמצע - הא ר"ש והא רבנן. וברייתא דקתני לא היה קושרה — מדאורייתא שרי, דס"ל לר"ש מכשירין דמצוה דוחין היכא דלא אפשר להו מאתמול; ומשום גזירה הוא דגזר אמצע אטו מן הצד, אבל בעלמא, דליכא למיגזר מידי — דחי:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:5:1.english: And if you wish, say: Both are in the middle - This [baraita is according to] Rabbi Shimon, and that [mishna is according to] the Rabbis. And [as for] the baraita, which taught that he would not tie it — by Torah law it is permitted, as Rabbi Shimon maintains that preparations for a mitzvah override [Shabbat] where it was not possible [to perform] them yesterday, and it is [only] because of a decree that he decreed [prohibiting tying in] the middle on account of the side. But generally, where there is nothing to decree, it overrides [Shabbat].

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:6:1.hebrew: יבלת - ורוא"ה. והוא מום לתמיד, שדוחה את השבת, כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ב) "או חרוץ או יבלת". יבלת דקרא קרינן יבלת — שאין שם דבר, אלא כמו חיגרת, דומיא דשבור — ולא כתיב שבר, ועורת נמי לא כתיב עיורון; אבל יבלת דמתני' הוא שם דבר של המום:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:6:1.english: A wart - *Verrue* [wart]. And it is a blemish for [an animal designated for] the daily offering, which overrides Shabbat, as it is written: (Leviticus 22:22) "Or having a cut, or a wart." As for the *yavelet* of the verse, we read [it as] *yavelet* — for it is not a noun, but rather like *chigeret* [lame], similar to *shavur* [broken] — and it is not written *shever* [fracture] — and regarding *iveret* [blind] as well, it is not written *ivaron* [blindness]; but the *yavelet* of our Mishnah is the noun for the blemish.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:6:2.english: One may cut off a wart - [The Mishnah] means by hand.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:6:3.hebrew: אם בכלי כאן וכאן אסור - ואע"ג דכי עביד נמי ביד מתקן הוא, והוה ליה חותך מבעלי חיים, והוי תולדה דגוזז את הצמר — אפ"ה, כיון דכלאחר יד קא עביד, שאין כן דרך לחותכה אלא בסכין, אין כאן אלא שבות:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:6:3.english: If with an instrument, it is prohibited in both [places] - And even though when one does [it] by hand as well, he is rectifying [the animal or priest], and it is [considered] cutting from a living creature and is a derivative of shearing wool — nevertheless, since he does [it] in an abnormal manner [kel’aḥar yad], as it is not the usual way to cut it except with a knife, there is only a rabbinic prohibition [shevut] here.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:6:4.hebrew: ואם בכלי כאן וכאן אסור - דאב מלאכה הוי, הואיל ואינו משנה מכמות שעושין בחול:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:6:4.english: And if with an instrument, it is prohibited in both [places] - For it is a primary category of labor, since he does not alter [his action] from the way it is done on a weekday.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:7:1.hebrew: הרכיבו - בפסח הבא בשבת קאמר: הרכיבו על כתיפו ברה"ר, או להביאו מחוץ לתחום:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:7:1.english: Carrying it - It is speaking of a Paschal offering that occurs on Shabbat: carrying it on one's shoulder in the public domain, or bringing it from outside the [Shabbat] boundary.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:7:2.english: And cutting off its wart does not override - [It is] difficult: [one] anonymous [mishnah] against [another] anonymous [mishnah].

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:8:1.hebrew: הא - דפסחים בכלי, וה"נ קאמר תנא דמתניתין. ור"א אפילו בכלי שרי, דס"ל מכשירי מצוה דוחין שבת — כגון מלאכה שאפשר לעשותה מבעוד יום, כגון בקור המום — מכשירי קרבן הוא, והקרבן דוחה השבת, ובמכשירין פליגי:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:8:1.english: That - That [mishna] in Pesachim [refers to cutting the wart] with an instrument, and so too says the Tanna of our mishna. And Rabbi Eliezer permits [it] even with an instrument, for he holds [that] the prerequisites of a mitzvah override Shabbat; [even] a labor that could have been performed while it was still day, such as inspecting [for] a blemish, is a prerequisite of the sacrifice, and the sacrifice overrides Shabbat, and [so] they disagree regarding prerequisites.

Rashi on Eruvin 103a:9:1.hebrew: ביבישה - ואפ"ה בכלי אסור, משום דמתקן לה וענין מלאכה קא עביד. ודפסחים בלחה, ותרוייהו ביד:
Rashi on Eruvin 103a:9:1.english: In [the case of] a dry [wart] - And even so, [removing it] with an instrument is forbidden, because he repairs it and is performing an act of labor. And that [mishna] of Pesachim [deals] with a moist [wart], and both of them [refer to removing it] by hand.

Tosafot on Eruvin 103a:10:1.hebrew: הא בלחה הא ביבישה - [מתניתין ביבישה], ואפילו הכי אסרינן בכלי, דשבות גדול הוא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 103a:10:1.english: "This is referring to a moist [wart] and that is referring to a dry [one]" - [Our Mishnah is referring to a dry wart,] and even so we prohibit [cutting it] with an instrument, because it is a major rabbinic prohibition.

Tosafot on Eruvin 103a:10:2.hebrew: יבישה אפילו בכלי שרי - ולא מסתבר להחמיר עליו, כיון דאפרוכי מפריך:
Tosafot on Eruvin 103a:10:2.english: A dry [wart] is permitted even with an instrument - And it is not reasonable to be stringent regarding it, since it crumbles.

Tosafot on Eruvin 103a:18:1.hebrew: ולאו אוקימנא באסקופה כרמלית - תימה, דאמר לעיל (עירובין דף צז.) גבי מצאן צבתים או כריכות: מביאן פחות פחות מד' אמות — אלמא שבות דמקדש במדינה התירו! וי"ל, דשבות כי האי גוונא ודאי, שמוטלין בבזיון, התירו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 103a:18:1.english: "And didn’t we establish [it] as referring to a threshold that is a karmelit?" - This is puzzling, as [the Gemara] says above (Eruvin 97a) regarding [one who] found them in bundles or rolls: "He brings them [in] less than four cubits at a time" — which implies that a rabbinic prohibition relating to the Temple was permitted in the rest of the country! And it can be answered that a rabbinic prohibition of this sort, where they are certainly lying in disgrace, they permitted.
